sense: what is real, as against appearance or imitation

terms.gloss: reality, real life (as against imitation, appearance or opinion)
evidence: Cic. de Or. 3.215: in omnī rē vincit imitātiōnem vēritās (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “reality, real life, esp. of the likeness of life in works of art”. The same word is truth (see truth). For what really happened, as against what was said, see fact (rēs) and actually (rē vērā).

terms.gloss: the nature of things: the world as it really is
evidence: Cic. Ac. 2.55: quod rērum nātūra nōn patitur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: What the world allows or contains; in rērum nātūrā esse is to exist (see exist).

phrases.latin: vulgus ex vēritāte pauca, ex opīniōne multa aestimat
phrases.english: the crowd judges few things by reality and many by opinion

phrases.latin: in omnī rē vincit imitātiōnem vēritās
phrases.english: in everything the real thing beats the imitation

sources: Lewis & Short: veritas · Lewis & Short: natura
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
